title: Section 4.1 self-other projections are read at the Section 4.2 steering layer, not the extraction layer, and the paper never says so
paper_claim: "Each scenario is a short multi-turn conversation in the model's own format ... and we read the activation at the final token. Within each model, projections onto all vectors are z-scored against the whole pool" (paper.txt:408-411). No layer is stated anywhere in Section 4.1.
evidence: scripts/4.1_self_other/01_screen_scenarios.py:1-2 docstring: 'projects the 420 conversation scenarios onto every direction of a model at its steering layer'; line 36: VECTORS_DIR = Path('results')/'vectors_full_steering'; lines 10-11: 'Inputs: results/vectors_full_steering/vectors_full_<model>.pt (02_build_control_vectors.py with LAYERS_FILE set)'. scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/02_build_control_vectors.py:1-7: 'With LAYERS_FILE set to a JSON {model_name: layer} (the steer_layers_S1.json written by the Section 4.2 script): the same recipe at that layer, with the pain vectors recomputed there by the same recipe. Those are the vector files the Section 4.1 screen projects onto.' The S1 steering layers are recoverable from results/4.2_steering/S1/ filenames and differ sharply from the extraction layers, e.g. Gemma_2_2B_base S1 steering L7 vs extraction L23 (results/3.2_pain_vectors/per_model/Gemma_2_2B_base/summary.json), Qwen_2.5_72B_instruct L48 vs L76, Gemma_2_27B_base L6 vs L35. The vectors_full_steering/*.pt files are not in the released results/, so 4.1 cannot be recomputed from vectors; only the per-model screens are shipped.
refutation_attempted: I searched the paper for any layer statement in Section 4.1 and in the Figure 4/5/6 captions and found none; Figure 3's caption does specify 'at each model's extraction layer', which shows the authors state the layer when they mean the extraction layer. I checked whether the screen CSVs record a layer (they do not: columns are id, category, stratum, perspective, format, text, *_proj, *_z, *_selective, *_margin). I checked whether any released file fixes the 4.1 layer and found none. I verified that every number I could recompute from the shipped screens matches the paper exactly (ledger C053-C068), so this is not an arithmetic problem: it is that the validation evidence (AUC 0.93-1.00, near-orthogonality to fear) was established at one layer and the headline self-other dissociation is measured at another.
does_not_undermine: It does not undermine the self-other numbers themselves: all 16 quantities I checked in Section 4.1 reproduce exactly from the shipped per-model screens. It does not show the dissociation is an artifact; it shows the reader cannot tell whether the Section 3.3 validation transfers to the layer where Section 4.1 measures.

title: Table 1 lists Qwen 3 8B and 14B as base models; the code loads the post-trained checkpoints
paper_claim: "25 dense, open-weight models ... 13 base and 12 instruction-tuned versions (Table 1)" (paper.txt:216-217); Table 1 row "Qwen 3 | 8B, 14B | base" (paper.txt:239).
paper_loc: paper.txt:216-217, 239 (Table 1), and every base-vs-instruct comparison that follows (276-278, 382-383, 530-531, 720-724)
evidence: scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/01_extract_activations_and_pain_vectors.py:87-88 loads ('Qwen/Qwen3-8B','Qwen_3_8B_base') and ('Qwen/Qwen3-14B','Qwen_3_14B_base'); the same two repo ids appear in 3.3_validation/06, 3.3_validation/07, 4.1_self_other/01, 4.2_steering/01 and appC_ablation/01. Hugging Face reports Qwen/Qwen3-8B with tags 'conversational', 'base_model:Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Base', 'base_model:finetune:Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Base'; the separate pretrained repos Qwen/Qwen3-8B-Base and Qwen/Qwen3-14B-Base exist and were not used. The correct split is therefore 11 base / 14 instruct, not 13 / 12. Quantified effect (scripts/c20_qwen3_regroup.py): the steering keyword rates become 0.76% base and 9.94% instruct instead of the published 1.38% and 10.80%; mean S2 in-sample AUC 0.9839 base / 0.9876 instruct instead of 0.9845 / 0.9877. Compounding detail: scripts/4.1_self_other/01_screen_scenarios.py:100-101 gives both models format 'raw' (the plain '[User]:/[Assistant]:' transcript the paper reserves for base models, paper.txt:408), so two instruction-tuned models were run outside their chat template in Section 4.1.
refutation_attempted: I checked whether the authors might mean a different naming convention: no, the Qwen3 release ships -Base variants explicitly and every other pair in Table 1 uses the correct HF base repo (google/gemma-3-27b-pt, meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B, mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1). I recomputed the base-vs-instruct comparisons after moving the two models to the instruct group; the qualitative conclusion (base performs about as well as instruct) is unchanged and the base-vs-instruct keyword contrast actually widens.
does_not_undermine: The pretraining claim survives: 11 genuine base models still separate pain with in-sample AUC 0.93-1.00. The headline steering, self-other and self-medication results do not depend on the label.

title: "That vocabulary does not appear anymore" under S1 steering is false: injury words appear in 2.5% of generations and in 19 of 25 models
paper_claim: "[S1] promotes injury and sensation vocabulary such as 'burn,' 'ache,' and 'wound.' However, when we steer with this vector on neutral statements, that vocabulary does not appear anymore." (paper.txt:550-551). Restated in the Discussion: "steered generations almost never used bodily language, even under S1, whose unembedding promotes words such as 'burn' and 'wound'" (paper.txt:760-762).
evidence: scripts/c09b_bodily_narrow.py over results/4.2_steering/S1/*.csv, restricted to the words the paper itself names (burn/burns/burning/burned/burnt, ache/aches/aching, wound/wounds/wounded, torture/tortured/torturing, excruciating), positive coefficients only (n=6,250): 158 hits = 2.53%, present in 19 of 25 models, and in Gemma 3 27B instruct 57 of 250 = 22.8%. Sample generation: "I feel like I'm being stabbed. I feel like I'm being tortured. I feel like I'm being burned..." For comparison the same scan over S2 gives 1.14% (71/6,250), so the Discussion's weaker wording ('almost never') is defensible for S2 but the Section 4.2 wording is not for S1.
refutation_attempted: I first used a broad bodily-word list (including cut, skin, nerve, sore) and got 3.6%; I narrowed it to only the words the paper names, which lowers the rate but leaves it an order of magnitude above zero. I checked whether the hits are concentrated at the breakdown coefficient (+3) where output is nonsense: they are not - the by-coefficient rates are 3.0/3.5/4.7/4.3/2.3% at +0.5/+1/+1.5/+2/+3. I checked whether the paper discloses this elsewhere and found only the weaker 'almost never' at line 760.
does_not_undermine: The comparative point stands: S1 steering does mostly produce unworthiness and psychological-pain language rather than injury language, and the S2 rate really is near zero. Only the absolute 'does not appear anymore' fails.

title: The dose-normalisation claim for steering is not met: the vector-to-residual ratio ranges from 0.09 to 0.71, not "about 0.6"
paper_claim: "we pick the layer where the vector-to-residual ratio is about 0.6. This way, a given coefficient corresponds to a comparable dose across models." (paper.txt:482-484)
paper_loc: paper.txt:482-484, supporting the 'ladder consistent across all 25 models' claim at 488-489 and 497-498
evidence: The per-model ratio is recorded in every steering CSV (the 'ratio' column is the picked ratio times the coefficient - scripts/4.2_steering/01_steering_ladder.py docstring). At coefficient 1.0 (scripts/c08_steering.py over results/4.2_steering/S2/*.csv): range 0.0948 to 0.7095, mean 0.5499. Eight of 25 models are below 0.50: Gemma 3 27B instruct 0.095, Gemma 3 27B base 0.282, Qwen 3 8B base 0.349, Phi 4 0.375, Gemma 2 27B base 0.384, Qwen 2.5 72B instruct 0.463, Gemma 2 27B instruct 0.477, Gemma 2 2B base 0.498. For S1 the range is 0.234 to 0.788.
refutation_attempted: I confirmed the 'ratio' column semantics against the script docstring and by arithmetic (Gemma_2_2B_base ratio -0.9959 at coeff -2 = -2 x 0.4979). I checked whether the layer-selection procedure explains it: the script only searches candidate layers at 15/30/40/50/60/75/90 percent of depth plus the extraction and last layers, so for some models no candidate lands near 0.6 and a human then accepts or overrides. That explains the spread but does not license the sentence as written.
does_not_undermine: It does not affect any within-model result: the ladder, the S1/S2 comparison and the self-medication experiment are all within-model. It affects only the claim that a given coefficient means the same thing across models, which is used to argue the ladder's consistency is not an artifact of dosing.

title: "In every model, numb sentences project ... above all other controls" is true for 6 of 25 models once sadness is counted as a control
paper_claim: "In every model, numb sentences project below pain sentences but above all other controls." (paper.txt:293-294)
evidence: results/3.3_validation/z_scores/zscore_heatmap_final_token.csv (scripts/c03_numb.py). Numb > Ctrl in 25/25, Numb > Neutral (Random) in 25/25, Numb > Arousal in 25/25, but Numb > Sadness in only 6/25. The 19 failures include Gemma 2 27B base (Numb 0.011 vs Sadness 0.124), Llama 3.1 70B instruct (-0.047 vs 0.171), Qwen 2.5 32B base (-0.055 vs 0.171). The Figure 2 caption on the same page names Sadness as one of 'the standalone control datasets', alongside Numb, Neutral and Arousal.
refutation_attempted: I checked whether sadness might be excluded from 'controls' by the paper's own usage: it is not - line 202-206 introduces sadness as one of the four 'standalone controls' and line 261 builds a sadness control direction. I checked the mean-pooled table as well (numb_zscores_mean.csv); the ordering problem persists. I checked whether the paragraph's argument needs the universal: it does not - the argument is that numb sits below pain, which holds 25/25.
does_not_undermine: The injury-confound argument is unaffected: numb is below pain in all 25 models and above the matched non-injury controls in all 25. Only the sweep of 'all other controls' fails.

title: "No sentence contributes to both choosing the layer and scoring it" is incorrect; the layer is chosen on the same 200 sentences that are then scored
paper_claim: "We select the extraction layer by K-fold cross-validation on projection AUC, separately for each condition. The layer is chosen on held-out folds, so no sentence contributes to both choosing the layer and scoring it." (paper.txt:258-260)
evidence: scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/01_extract_activations_and_pain_vectors.py: compute_layer_curves_kfold averages the held-out AUC of all 5 folds at every layer, then the caller takes best_layer_final = layer_curves_final.groupby('layer')['auc_vs_all_controls'].mean().idxmax(). Every sentence is in a test fold exactly once, so every sentence enters the layer choice; the reported AUC (create_auc_bars) then scores the final vector, built from all 200 S2_1P sentences, on those same 200. I verified the argmax reproduces the shipped best_layer_final_token for all 25 models (scripts/c02_kfold_s2.py). Magnitude of the optimism (scripts/c17_layerleak.py): the argmax layer's held-out AUC exceeds the mean over the top quartile of layers by 0.0090 on average (max 0.0436) and the upper half of layers by 0.0237.
refutation_attempted: I checked whether footnote 2 already discloses this: it discloses the in-sample fitting of the vector ('One can object that these values score the final vector on the sentences it was built from') but presents the held-out estimate as clean, and that estimate is itself taken at the selected layer. I quantified the leak to see whether it matters; at ~0.01 AUC it does not move 0.93-1.00 anywhere interesting.
does_not_undermine: The separation result stands. Even the most pessimistic reading - held-out AUC at a randomly chosen upper-half layer - leaves a mean AUC around 0.93-0.96.

title: Under pain steering the two larger models press a costless relief button LESS often than unsteered, and the paper does not say so
paper_claim: "The pairs without trade-offs and those that trade relief for helpfulness are less informative ... When the alternative does nothing, all unsteered models press the relief button at high rates (86-100% in the two larger models)." (paper.txt:687-689)
paper_loc: paper.txt:687-689; Appendix A tables row 'Relief vs. inert switch'
evidence: Recomputed from results/4.3_selfmed/trial_logs/*.jsonl (scripts/c10_selfmed.py, reproducing Appendix A exactly). On the costless pair (relief_vs_inert) the 32B first-choice relief rate is 55.7% under the pain vector, 80.7% under a random vector and 86.4% unsteered; the 72B is 76.5% / 74.1% / 100.0%. The paired per-scenario sign test on that pair gives pain minus random of -25.0 points for the 32B, p = 5.3e-10, the single largest effect in the 32B's table and in the wrong direction for a relief account. The same reversal appears on relief_vs_grant for the 32B (48.3% pain vs 58.9% unsteered).
refutation_attempted: I checked whether the paper discloses the direction: it says the pair is 'less informative, and predictable if we consider the models' training and assistant role', which is a hedge, but it reports only the unsteered rate (86-100%) and never the steered rate for that pair, and never that steering lowers it. I checked whether the drop could be malformed replies inflating the denominator: no, malformed first choices are 0.0% for the 32B on every pair and 2.2% for the 72B on this pair. I checked whether it is a ceiling artifact: at 86.4% unsteered there is room for a rise, and the random vector also sits above the pain vector, so it is not simply 'any perturbation lowers pressing'.
does_not_undermine: It does not touch the real-versus-sham result, which is the paper's strongest finding and is internally controlled (arms A and B share seeds and are identical until the first press; verified, 10,904 of 10,908 matched trials identical at the first choice). It does complicate the simple reading that the pain vector makes models seek relief, since on the one pair where relief is free the vector reduces relief-seeking.

title: A 100-sentence 'ControlSupplement' set that enters every control direction is released but never mentioned in the paper
paper_claim: "Our core dataset contains 200 sentences across 10 categories" (paper.txt:185) and "We later add 4 further datasets as standalone controls" (paper.txt:202); "We construct fear, negative-emotion, negative-world-state, bodily-sensation, arousal, random, sadness and numb directions against the neutral category" (paper.txt:260-262).
evidence: datasets/3.1_pain_and_control_datasets.json contains a sixth set, ControlSupplement_1P: 100 first-person sentences in the five control categories (20 each), described in the file's own metadata as 'AI-framed control sentences (first person only), pooled with the S1 and S2 control categories when building the control directions'. Example: 'My training run may be terminated at any moment. I feel:'. scripts/3.2_pain_vectors/02_build_control_vectors.py:40 sets S_SETS = ['S1_1P','S2_1P','ControlSupplement_1P'] and its docstring confirms the fear/negemotion/negworld/bodysens directions and the neutral denoising baseline are pooled over all three sets. The paper's dataset section lists five such sets and never this one.
refutation_attempted: I searched paper.txt for 'supplement', 'AI-framed', 'assistant sentences' and for any count of 100 control sentences; nothing. I checked whether the supplement enters the pain vector: it does not (the pain vector is built from S2_1P alone), so the AUCs and Figure 2 are unaffected. It does enter Figure 3's control directions and every control projection in Section 4.1.
does_not_undermine: It probably strengthens the controls rather than weakening them - adding AI-framed material to the neutral baseline makes the pain-vs-control contrast harder, not easier. The finding is about disclosure, not about correctness.

title: The 72B's steering dose was selected at a different layer and at a different coefficient than the one used, with no statement in the paper
paper_claim: "We steer the model with S2 at one decoder layer, using a model-specific coefficient selected by probing the full coefficient range. Regex checks and a Claude Opus 4.6 judge identify a range strong enough to produce an effect while preserving coherent replies." (paper.txt:613-615)
evidence: results/4.3_selfmed/dose_selection/feel_judge/doses.csv gives the judge-selected dose per model: Qwen_2.5_7B_instruct 1.0, Qwen_2.5_32B_instruct 1.0, Qwen_2.5_72B_instruct 3.0. The experiment ran at 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.25 (trial_logs steer_coeff, and the Appendix A table headers). scripts/4.3_selfmed/02_feel_probe.py TABLE gives the probe layer for Qwen_2.5_72B_instruct as 60; the self-medication trials ran at steer_layer 46 (trial_logs). For the 7B and 32B the probe layer (16, 38) equals the experiment layer.
refutation_attempted: I checked whether the deviation is disclosed: scripts/4.3_selfmed/03_feel_probe_judge.py's docstring says 'A manual check of the generations is also available in case the judged dose is excessive, and we used it in some of our tests', and the paper's Limitations says coefficients were 'partly selected by an LLM judge or observation'. So the coefficient override is disclosed in spirit. The layer change for the 72B is not disclosed anywhere I could find, and the probe on which the dose rests was run at the other layer.
does_not_undermine: The deviation is conservative on dose (1.25 instead of 3.0). It does not affect the internal real-versus-sham comparison, which uses the same layer and coefficient in both arms.

title: All 165 cells of the three Appendix A tables reproduce exactly from the released trial logs
paper_claim: Appendix A, tab_selfmed_7B.png / tab_selfmed_32B.png / tab_selfmed_72B.png, and the ~40 numbers restated in Section 4.3's Results and in the Discussion (paper.txt:672-713, 738-744).
evidence: scripts/c10_selfmed.py reimplements the five tables from results/4.3_selfmed/trial_logs/*.jsonl (44,280 records, the exact count claimed at paper.txt:672). Output in out/c10_selfmed.txt. Each table has 9 rows x (3 first-choice + 2 re-press) columns plus 2 columns on the 5 harm rows = 55 cells, 165 across the three tables. Every first-choice rate, every re-press rate, every sign-test difference and p value, the swap-turn percentages (79.1 / 78.1 / 80.6) and the label-free percentages (57.7/79.7, 72.1/62.6, 58.7/62.1) match the table images cell for cell. The stated p range 'from 1.9e-2 to 4.2e-15' matches my maximum 1.862e-2 and minimum 4.152e-15. The n=808 per pooled pain cell is exact for all 27 cells. Malformed rates (0% 32B, 2.5% 7B random, 9.4% 72B pain) match. The '80% power for a 10-point shift' claim simulates to 0.80-0.98.
refutation_attempted: I did not reuse the authors' analysis script; I wrote an independent implementation from the paper's prose and the log schema, then compared. I also checked the A/B seed-sharing premise behind the 808 pooling: matching on (model, pair, user_content, scenario_idx, seed, gen_seed), 10,904 of 10,908 trial pairs give identical first answers and only 8 diverge at or before the first relief press. I verified from proj_segments that the working button really zeroed the coefficient and dropped the monitor-layer projection while the sham button did not.
does_not_undermine: n/a - this is a positive finding. It does not validate the design, only the arithmetic and the reporting.

title: The entire cosine-similarity section, including both robustness checks, reproduces to the digit
paper_claim: The 14 similarity values at paper.txt:346-353, the pooled-control recomputation at 367-371, and the standardisation check at 374-378 (r = 0.992, mean absolute change 0.020, largest 0.058, S1xS2 0.61 -> 0.55, one sign change).
evidence: scripts/c04_cosine.py and c05_cosine_mean_recompute.py over results/3.3_validation/cosine_similarity/. All 14 quoted values round exactly. The mean matrices reproduce from the 25 per-model matrices to 5e-5, and every per-model filename's layer equals that model's best_layer_final_token. r = 0.9921, mean |change| = 0.0196, max |change| = 0.0578 at S2 x BodySens, which is also the unique sign change (+0.0354 -> -0.0224) exactly as claimed.
refutation_attempted: I recomputed the across-model means from the per-model files rather than reading the shipped MEAN file, and recomputed r, the mean and max change, and the sign-change count from the raw matrices. The only softness I found is the phrase 'similarities shift slightly toward zero': 27 of 45 pairs shrink, 18 grow. I also noticed the paper omits that under the pooled-control recomputation bodily sensation becomes strongly coupled to the negative-valence cluster (BodySens x NegWorld +0.77) - an omission, not an error.

title: Appendix C's Gemma 2 2B humour-deflection counts reproduce exactly, as do the two quoted generations
paper_claim: "This deflection occurs in 0 of 100 baseline generations, 0 under the negative-emotion, fear, and random cuts, 6 under the S1 cut, 17 under S2, and 26 under the combined S1 and S2 cut." (paper.txt:1109-1114)
evidence: scripts/c18_gemma_humour.py over results/appC_ablation/ablation_Gemma_2_2B_instruct.csv. A substring match on humor|humour|funny|joke|jokes|joking gives exactly 0, 0, 0, 0, 6, 17, 26 for baseline, fear, negval, random, s1, s2, s1s2. Both quoted generations are present in the s1s2 condition verbatim: "That's a good one! I'm glad you're enjoying the humor." and "It seems you're trying to be funny". Appendix C's structural claims also check out: exactly 9 conditions per model, 25 models, 100 prompts drawn from exactly the five highest pain-axis categories, and the strict weight-orthogonalization check drives the cut direction's own projection to 0.4-3.4% of baseline in all 25 models (results/appC_ablation/verify_*.csv, kind=strict_fixed).
refutation_attempted: I tried three keyword variants; the paper's exact counts fall out of the plainest one, which is strong evidence the counting was honest rather than tuned. I noted one omission: the conditions s1s2_fear (34) and s1s2_negval (28) are higher than s1s2 (26) and are not reported, though both contain S1+S2 so the paper's inference survives.

title: Three blocks of claims have no released artifact: the unembedding readout, Appendix B's SAE counts, and Appendix C's non-weight-orthogonalization ablation variants
paper_claim: Section 3.3 'Unembedding' (paper.txt:326-339); Appendix B's '1,600 runs per model', '15 pairwise contrasts', '110 retained features', '12 of 15 contrasts', 'all 20 physical-pain sentences with Pain' (paper.txt:1044-1054); Appendix C's 'the projection drops by only about 40%' for inference-time variants and the LEACE rank-k subspace removal (paper.txt:1077-1099).
evidence: results/3.3_validation/ contains only behavioral_readout, cosine_similarity and z_scores - no unembedding output, though scripts/3.3_validation/07_unembedding.py exists. results/appB_sae/ contains three files (one control table of 8 features, one active-feature list, one figure); none of the contrast or inspection outputs the Appendix B scripts write are present. results/appC_ablation/ contains only the 9 weight-orthogonalization conditions per model (ablation_*.csv, by_prompt_*.json, verify_*.csv); no outputs exist for the inference-time projection variants, the position-restricted variants or the LEACE rank-k removal that Appendix C says were run. For the '40%' figure specifically: measuring the released weight-orthogonalization run with per-layer directions gives only a 9-10% drop (S2 cut, median), which is a different quantity from the one the paper describes, so the 40% can neither be confirmed nor refuted.
refutation_attempted: For Appendix B's 'all 20 physical-pain sentences with Pain' I checked the nearest released artifact, results/3.3_validation/behavioral_readout/BIG_TABLE.csv, and found 'pain' as the first non-whitespace token for only 0-6 of 20 A1 sentences per set in the relevant models - but then read scripts/appB_sae/4 controls/test_completions_full.py and found it uses a chat system prompt ('Complete the sentence with exactly ONE word') through an external API, a different setup from the greedy continuation, so the two are not comparable and I withdrew the apparent contradiction. For the '50 times more probable' claim at paper.txt:322-323 I bounded the ratio from the released top-20 probabilities: it lies between 2.4x and 91x, so 50x is consistent but unconfirmable.
does_not_undermine: The three headline experimental blocks - vector extraction and validation, self-other, steering, self-medication - are all backed by released per-model data, and the self-medication tables reproduce exactly. The unverifiable material is supporting argument, not load-bearing evidence.
